name: espos
summary: EspOS developer tools: make, check and run packages (.espk) in the simulator, QEMU or on a board.

exit_codes.1: the command ran and found problems or a step failed
exit_codes.3: a tool or file the command needs is missing
exit_codes.4: no EspOS S3 found, or a serial port refused for safety

output: Human text on stdout, warnings and progress on stderr; with --json (commands marked json) stdout carries exactly one JSON document.

environment.ESPOS_ROOT: the s3desk firmware repo (default: found by walking up for platformio.ini + src/)
environment.ESPOS_PYTHON: python3 to run the repo's tools
environment.ESPOS_PORT: the serial port of the EspOS S3 (it must still answer as kind s3)
environment.ESPOS_DENY_PORTS: serial ports never opened, comma separated (also deny_ports in config.json; none by default)
environment.ESPOS_SIM_BUILD: the simulator's build folder name under sim/ (default build, build-live for --live)
environment.ESPOS_BBK: the store upload key, read only by scripts/publish_pkg.py (store publish --yes)
environment.ESPOS_PUBLISH_SCRIPT: scripts/publish_pkg.py if it is not next to s3desk

global_options.name: --json
global_options.description: Machine-readable output on stdout (commands marked json).

global_options.name: --root
global_options.description: The s3desk firmware repo (default: found from the current folder or the CLI's own place).

commands.name: create
commands.summary: Make a new package project from a template.

args.name: dir
args.description: the folder to create (its name is the default display name)

options.name: --template
options.description: the kind of project

options.name: --id
options.description: package id, reverse domain (default com.example.<dir>, jar.<name> for games); never changes once published

options.name: --name
options.description: display name (at most 40 characters, no "…")

options.name: --desc
options.description: one line for the store (at most 300 characters)

options.name: --author
options.description: author (at most 40 characters)

options.name: --category
options.description: store category

options.name: --jar
options.description: j2me-game: the game's .jar (fills name, version, MIDlet, icon)

options.name: --license
options.description: j2me-game: where the game comes from and its licence (required with --jar)

options.name: --keypad
options.description: j2me-game: the suggested keypad

options.name: --force
options.description: write into a folder that is not empty

notes: js-app: JavaScript app (main.js, API level 1): a counter that keeps its number
js-app-ts: TypeScript app (src/*.ts bundled into main.js, typed by @espos/sdk): a countdown with a reminder
j2me-game: a J2ME (Java phone) game wrapped as a package: game.jar + icon, engine j2me (firmware 0.4.0)
No widget, face, theme, service or driver templates: those package types need manifest v2 (planned, docs/platform.md), which no firmware reads yet.
examples: espos create focus-timer --template js-app-ts --id vn.you.focus --name "Focus timer"
espos create megablock --template j2me-game --jar MegaBlock.jar --license "Apache-2.0, xylophones.net"

commands.name: build
commands.summary: Bundle (TypeScript), check and write the .espk.
commands.description: A project (espos.json) packs its main (bundled with esbuild when it is TypeScript) and its files; a plain folder with manifest.json packs every file but dotfiles and hidden folders, exactly as tools/espk.py does (byte-identical output). Nothing is written when a check fails.

options.name: --out
options.description: the .espk to write (default: <out>/<id>-<version>-<part>.espk; for a plain folder, next to it)

options.name: --out-dir
options.description: the folder to write it to

options.name: --typecheck
options.description: type-check TypeScript (--no-typecheck to skip)

options.name: --minify
options.description: minify the bundled main.js

options.name: --strict
options.description: warnings fail the build too

commands.name: check
commands.summary: Check packages: manifest, files, icon, sizes, permissions vs the APIs the code calls.
commands.description: The one validator: every rule of tools/espk.py, scripts/publish_pkg.py, the web admin and the device (src/pkg/espk.cpp), the strictest where they differ, plus checks of main.js (syntax, permissions, API level 1). Folders are built in memory first; .espk files with the same id are checked together as the parts of one package.

options.name: --strict
options.description: warnings fail too

options.name: --typecheck
options.description: type-check TypeScript projects (--no-typecheck to skip)

options.name: --rules
options.description: list the rules (code, level, what, where it comes from)

commands.name: inspect
commands.summary: Show what is inside an .espk: manifest, files, offsets, CRCs, sha256, its catalog entry.

options.name: --base
options.description: base URL for the catalog entry's part URLs

options.name: --extract
options.description: also unpack the files and manifest.json into DIR

commands.name: jar
commands.summary: Wrap a J2ME game (.jar) into a game package (engine j2me), as the web admin does.
commands.description: Reads META-INF/MANIFEST.MF (MIDlet-Name, -Vendor, -Version, MIDlet-1, MIDlet-Icon, profile, configuration), makes the icon a 120x120 baseline JPEG on a tile of its average colour, and writes jar.<slug>-<version>-core.espk (kind native, engine j2me, min_fw 400, perms sound). The licence text is required.

options.name: --license

options.name: --keypad

options.name: --version

options.name: --code
options.description: version code (default from the version: 1.2.3 = 10203)

options.name: --out
options.description: the .espk to write

options.name: --out-dir
options.description: the folder for <id>-<version>-core.espk (default .)

options.name: --project
options.description: write a project folder (manifest.json, espos.json, game.jar, icon.jpg) instead of an .espk

options.name: --force

commands.name: store
commands.summary: Catalog entries and publishing to the store (wraps scripts/publish_pkg.py).

commands.name: entry
commands.summary: Print the catalog "packages" entry for the parts of a package (tools/espk.py --entry with publish_pkg.py's part rules).

options.name: --base

commands.name: publish
commands.summary: Check, then publish packages with scripts/publish_pkg.py. Without --yes it is a dry run.
commands.description: Runs the validator first (refuses on errors), then publish_pkg.py. The upload key is read only from the environment variable ESPOS_BBK by publish_pkg.py itself; espos never takes it as an argument, prints it or stores it. Without --yes, publish_pkg.py --dry-run prints the plan and the merged catalog.

options.name: --yes
options.description: really upload (needs ESPOS_BBK in the environment)

options.name: --dry-run
options.description: only print the plan (the default without --yes)

options.name: --catalog
options.description: merge into this local catalog.json instead of the live one (offline check)

options.name: --out
options.description: also write the merged catalog to FILE

options.name: --replace
options.description: allow the same version again with other bytes

options.name: --shot
options.description: a store screenshot (baseline JPEG)

options.name: --meta
options.description: part choices from a build tool's catalog entry

notes: Needs python3 and ../scripts/publish_pkg.py next to s3desk (or ESPOS_PUBLISH_SCRIPT).

commands.name: sim
commands.summary: Run packages in the SDL simulator: install, build the simulator if needed, open the app.
commands.description: Builds project folders (or takes .espk files), installs them into a simulator data folder (by default <project>/.espos/sim-data-live, a copy of s3/sim/data-live), builds the simulator with make when its sources changed, and runs it with a script that opens the first app. Headless runs write PNG screenshots and exit 1 when the app throws ("app <id>: ..." in the trace). JavaScript apps go to the device's flash (fs/pkgs), other packages to the card; Java games get the J2ME runtime from build-pkgs/.

args.name: targets
args.description: project folders or .espk files (default: the current folder if it has manifest.json)

options.name: --live
options.description: the window (the default; mouse = finger, keys, sound): sim/build-live/espos-live

options.name: --headless
options.description: no window, script time, screenshots, exit 1 on an app error (CI): sim/build/espos-sim

options.name: --script
options.description: simulator commands run after the app opens (default: <project>/sim/smoke.txt)

options.name: --app
options.description: the app to open (default: the first package)

options.name: --arg
options.description: app.arg for the opened app

options.name: --open
options.description: open the app (--no-open: only install and boot)

options.name: --data
options.description: the simulator data folder to use (default <project>/.espos/sim-<base>)

options.name: --base
options.description: what a new data folder is copied from: data-live, data-run, data or a folder

options.name: --fresh
options.description: start from a new copy of the base data

options.name: --vol
options.description: where to install: sd (the card) or flash (the device's flash, JavaScript only)

options.name: --out
options.description: screenshots (default <project>/.espos/shots)

options.name: --watch
options.description: rebuild, reinstall and restart (live) or run again (headless) when a file changes

options.name: --build
options.description: build the simulator when needed (--no-build: use the last binary)

options.name: --sim-build
options.description: the simulator's build folder under sim/

options.name: --fast
options.description: live: the computer's speed instead of the board's

options.name: --zoom
options.description: live: points per screen pixel

options.name: --board
options.description: 35 only: the 2.8" board (28) runs in QEMU (espos qemu --board 28)

options.name: --log
options.description: headless: print the simulator's whole log

options.name: --timeout
options.description: headless: stop after S seconds

options.name: --force
options.description: install even when the checks find errors

notes: --watch restarts the simulator: an app cannot be reloaded inside a running simulator yet.
Script commands (sim/main.cpp): tap X Y, long X Y, drag X0 Y0 X1 Y1 MS, swipe left|right|up|down, back, home, app ID [ARG], wait MS, shot NAME, set KEY VALUE, rot N, saver, wake, mem, quit.
macOS only today: the simulator uses malloc_zone_statistics (sim/main.cpp) and macOS frameworks (live window).

commands.name: qemu
commands.summary: Run the real firmware in Espressif's QEMU (tools/qemu/run.sh), with packages put onto its card.
commands.description: Wraps tools/qemu/run.sh: builds env s3desk-qemu (s3desk-28-qemu for --board 28), puts it into build-qemu/flash.bin keeping the device's data (NVS link token, LittleFS, the card), and runs QEMU with the viewer. --install puts packages onto the card image in place (mtools, or hdiutil on macOS) before QEMU starts; with --fresh (or no image yet) the image is made first from sim/data-live, then the packages are added.
commands.platform: macOS (run.sh's viewer and mkimage.py's card use macOS tools); QEMU from Espressif (esp-develop-9.2.2) in ../tools-ext/qemu or $QEMU

options.name: --board
options.description: 28 = the 2.8" board (its own image, card, console port 5556, web 8081)

options.name: --install
options.description: .espk (or project folder) to put onto the card

options.name: --fresh
options.description: a new image from sim/data-live (unlinked, the card made again)

options.name: --keep
options.description: the image as it is: no firmware build

options.name: --card
options.description: the card image to change (default build-qemu/sd[-28].img)

options.name: --sdl
options.description: QEMU's own window (no mouse), the dev console on this terminal

options.name: --tcp
options.description: QEMU's own window, the dev console on a TCP port (tools/qemu/console.py PORT "APP id")

options.name: --headless
options.description: no window, the dev console on port 5555 (5556 for --board 28)

options.name: --run
options.description: start QEMU (--no-run: only build/put the packages on the card)

options.name: --force
options.description: install even when the checks find errors

notes: The card image must not change while QEMU runs: --install refuses when its monitor socket answers.
Dev console in QEMU: APP <id>, TAP x y, DRAG ..., SHOT; screenshots: tools/qemu/console.py PORT shot:FILE.ppm.

commands.name: device
commands.summary: Talk to an EspOS S3 over USB: list, info, shot, logs, app, tap, drag, home, trace, mem, js, send, console.
commands.description: Port safety: ports are listed from the OS without opening them; a port is opened only to ask ESPOS:HELLO and used only if it answers ESPOS:READY with kind s3; ports on the deny list are never opened. Without --port, device commands open only an S3 remembered by its USB serial number or the default /dev/cu.usbmodem1101; `device list --probe` identifies other Espressif ports (and remembers the S3). No flashing here.
commands.platform: macOS and Linux; needs the optional npm package serialport

commands.name: firmware
commands.summary: Build the firmware (PlatformIO) and check firmware.bin against the 3,932,160-byte app slot.
commands.description: No flashing here: the board is flashed by its owner. The size check fails (exit 1) when firmware.bin is bigger than the app slot (app0 in the partition table, 0x3C0000).
